dmm-2008-relay-01.title: Factor
dmm-2008-relay-01.body:
$49^2+18^2=2401+324=2725=5^2\cdot109$, and $109$ is prime. The largest prime divisor is $109$.

**Answer: 109**

dmm-2008-relay-02.title: Compute both means
dmm-2008-relay-02.body:
This is relay problem 1B with $k=109$ (the answer to 1A). $L=89$. $m=\dfrac{87+100+92}{3}=93$ and $M=\dfrac{279+89}{4}=92$, so $m-M=1$.

**Answer: 1**

dmm-2008-relay-03.title: Count squares
dmm-2008-relay-03.body:
This is relay problem 1C with $k=1$ (the answer to 1B). $L=15\cdot2=30$. The perfect squares from $1$ to $30$ are $1,4,9,16,25$: five of them.

**Answer: 5**

dmm-2008-relay-04.title: Two presses are not enough
dmm-2008-relay-04.body:
Suppose the first press compares $k$ coins against $k$ coins ($k\le3$). There are two kinds of outcome.
- The scale tilts (say the left pan is heavier): the counterfeit is a heavy coin on the left or a light coin on the right, so there are $2k$ candidates, each with a known direction. One more press has only $3$ possible outcomes, so it can separate at most $3$ such candidates: we need $2k\le3$, i.e. $k=1$.
- The pans balance: the counterfeit is among the $7-2k$ coins left off, and we do not know whether it is heavy or light. One press can separate at most $2$ such candidates (weigh one of them against a known genuine coin). So we need $7-2k\le2$, i.e. $k\ge3$.

These requirements contradict each other, so $2$ presses cannot always succeed.

dmm-2008-relay-04.title: Three presses suffice
dmm-2008-relay-04.body:
Press 1: $\{1,2,3\}$ vs $\{4,5,6\}$. If balanced, coin $7$ is the counterfeit (done). Otherwise say the left side is heavier: then one of $1,2,3$ is heavy or one of $4,5,6$ is light, and coin $7$ is genuine.

Press 2: $\{1,2,5\}$ vs $\{3,4,7\}$. Left heavier $\Rightarrow$ counterfeit is $1$, $2$ (heavy) or $5$ (light). Right heavier $\Rightarrow$ it is $3$ (heavy) or $4$ (light). Balanced $\Rightarrow$ it is $6$.

Press 3: for $\{1,2,5\}$ weigh $1$ vs $2$: the heavier one is the counterfeit, and if balanced it is $5$. For $\{3,4\}$ weigh $3$ vs $7$: if they differ it is $3$, otherwise $4$.

**Answer: 3**

dmm-2008-relay-05.title: Vieta
dmm-2008-relay-05.body:
This is relay problem 2B with $k=3$ (the answer to 2A). By Vieta, $r+s+t=-2$ and $rs+st+tr=3$, so $r^2+s^2+t^2=(r+s+t)^2-2(rs+st+tr)=4-6=-2$ (the roots are not all real).

**Answer: $-2$**

dmm-2008-relay-06.title: Probabilities proportional to 1/p
dmm-2008-relay-06.body:
This is relay problem 2C with $k=-2$ (the answer to 2B). $L=\lfloor|-3|\rfloor=3$. The condition says $P(p)\cdot p$ is the same constant $c$ for all $p$, so $P(p)=c/p$ and $c\left(1+\frac12+\frac13+\frac14+\frac15+\frac16\right)=c\cdot\frac{49}{20}=1$, i.e. $c=\frac{20}{49}$. Then $P(3)=\frac{20}{49}\cdot\frac13=\frac{20}{147}$.

**Answer: $\dfrac{20}{147}$**
